q: For a specialised requirement, tenders are sent only to a restricted circle of approved and empanelled contractors instead of being advertised openly. This is the system of:

options.A: Open tenders
options.B: Single tenders
options.C: Limited tenders
options.D: Global tenders

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Inviting a single tender is an exception to the normal open tender system and requires the approval of the competent authority, with the reasons recorded.
2. Single tender may be resorted to as a matter of routine merely to save time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A contractor wishes to submit his bid for a railway work online and to receive the tender notice through the Railway's electronic portal. The system used for such online tendering is:

options.A: FOIS
options.B: IPAS
options.C: IRWCMS
options.D: IREPS

q: A government buyer needs a common-use good that is available on the Government e-Marketplace. Under the applicable procurement provisions, such goods and services available on GeM:

options.A: Are required to be procured through GeM itself by the government buyers
options.B: Can be procured only through open tenders
options.C: Cannot be procured by the Railways at all
options.D: Are procured only through registered agents

q: An accident has damaged a track structure and trains cannot run until it is restored, leaving no time to call tenders. Tenders may be dispensed with in such a genuine emergency on the basis of:

options.A: A verbal order of the sectional officer
options.B: The recommendation of a contractor already working in the section
options.C: A recorded urgency certificate by the competent authority
options.D: Approval of the tender committee after the work is done

q: A petty work of small value is to be arranged quickly, and the formal tender system is dispensed with for it. In such a case the work may be arranged on the basis of:

options.A: Advertisement in newspapers
options.B: Quotations obtained from contractors
options.C: Nomination by a contractor already working in the section
options.D: Verbal instructions of the sectional staff

q: Tenders for a work are due to be opened and some tenderers wish to witness the opening. Tenders are correctly opened:

options.A: Only after the tender committee submits its report
options.B: In the office of the contractor expected to be the lowest
options.C: After the Letter of Acceptance is issued
options.D: At the appointed date and time, in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as choose to be present

q: The Railway fails to communicate acceptance of a tender to the tenderer before the validity period of his tender expires. The consequence is that:

options.A: The tenderer is no longer bound by his offer and may withdraw it without forfeiture of the earnest money
options.B: The tender is deemed to have been accepted automatically
options.C: The earnest money is automatically forfeited
options.D: The validity is deemed to be extended indefinitely

q: A tenderer who has been awarded a work refuses to accept it and also fails to sign the agreement. In such a situation, the amount liable to be forfeited is his:

options.A: Performance guarantee
options.B: Security deposit
options.C: Earnest Money Deposit
options.D: Mobilisation advance

q: Tenders for a work have been finalised and the tenderers who did not succeed ask for the return of the earnest money they deposited with their tenders. The earnest money of unsuccessful tenderers is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in all cases
options.B: Refunded after finalisation of the tender
options.C: Converted into security deposit automatically
options.D: Adjusted against the first running bill of the successful tenderer

q: A tenderer asks at what stage he must furnish the Performance Guarantee for a work. The Performance Guarantee is required to be submitted by:

options.A: Every tenderer along with his tender
options.B: The tender committee before opening of tenders
options.C: Only contractors executing deposit works
options.D: The successful tenderer after issue of the Letter of Acceptance

q: A contractor who has satisfactorily completed his work and fulfilled all his contract obligations, including the maintenance period where applicable, becomes entitled to:

options.A: Release of the Performance Guarantee submitted by him
options.B: Payment of an additional mobilisation advance
options.C: Refund of the earnest money of all tenderers
options.D: Award of the next work without tender

q: A work is successfully completed, the final bill is settled and all dues and recoveries outstanding against the contractor are cleared. At this stage, the contractor becomes entitled to refund of his:

options.A: Earnest Money Deposit of the tender stage
options.B: Performance Guarantee alone, in all cases
options.C: Security Deposit
options.D: Secured advance

q: The Letter of Acceptance for a work is issued on a particular date and the successful contractor is called upon to furnish the Performance Guarantee. Ordinarily, the Performance Guarantee should be submitted by the contractor within:

options.A: 7 days of the Letter of Acceptance
options.B: 21 days of the Letter of Acceptance
options.C: 30 days of the Letter of Acceptance
options.D: 60 days of the Letter of Acceptance

q: While framing the tender conditions for a work, the executive wishes to know the ceiling up to which Earnest Money Deposit can be demanded from tenderers. In works tenders, the Earnest Money Deposit required from tenderers is subject to a maximum (cap) of:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 25 lakh
options.C: Rs 1 crore
options.D: Rs 50 lakh

q: A contractor brings costly durable materials to the site for incorporation in the work and seeks financial assistance against them before they are actually used. The advance that may be given against such materials brought to the site is a:

options.A: Secured advance
options.B: Mobilisation advance
options.C: Plant and machinery advance
options.D: Miscellaneous works advance

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mobilisation advance is paid to a contractor at the commencement of a work to enable him to mobilise men, materials and equipment for starting the work.
2. Mobilisation advance so paid is recovered from the contractor's subsequent on-account (running) bills.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A contractor brings brand-new plant and machinery to the site exclusively for use on a work and asks for an advance against it. Such an advance is granted:

options.A: Against the contractor's office furniture
options.B: Against new plant and machinery brought by the contractor to the site for use on the work
options.C: For purchase of vehicles for the Railway
options.D: Only after completion of the work

q: Earthwork for a foundation is about to be buried under the structure that will come up over it, and its quantity will thereafter be impossible to check. Such measurements, of work which will subsequently be covered up, should be:

options.A: Recorded after the covering work is completed
options.B: Estimated approximately at the time of the final bill
options.C: Recorded only if the contractor so demands
options.D: Recorded in the Measurement Book before the work is covered up

q: A dispute between the Railway and a works contractor cannot be settled amicably, and the contract provides a machinery for its resolution. In such a case the dispute is resolved through:

options.A: Arbitration, as provided in the General Conditions of Contract, under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
options.B: Direct decision of the Railway Board
options.C: Reference to the State Government
options.D: Recovery from the security deposit without further process

q: A concessionaire for a railway public-private partnership project reports that the debt and equity needed for the project have been tied up and the conditions for drawing the funds are in place. In project terminology, the stage so reached is called:

options.A: Commercial operation of the project
options.B: Issue of the completion certificate for the project
options.C: Handing over of the project to the authority
options.D: Financial closure of the project

q: Apart from publication in newspapers and on the Railways' own e-procurement portal, works tenders invited by the Railways are, under the General Financial Rules, also required to be published on:

options.A: The website of the State Government in which the work is located
options.B: The Central Public Procurement Portal
options.C: The website of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The notice board of the district court of the area

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Schedule of Powers of a zonal railway is framed on the basis of the Model Schedule of Powers issued by the Railway Board.
2. A delegated financial power can be exercised by an officer only within the monetary limits and subject to the conditions laid down in the delegation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Land acquired for a railway project is got mutated in the revenue records in favour of the Railways.
2. A zonal railway may, on its own authority, sell any railway land which it considers surplus to its requirements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The National Rail Plan drawn up by the Railways, with a vision horizon of 2030, is primarily aimed at:

options.A: Privatising the operation of all passenger trains
options.B: Fixing the freight rates chargeable for goods traffic
options.C: Preparing the cadre restructuring of railway officers
options.D: Creating railway capacity ahead of demand and increasing the modal share of the Railways in freight transport

q: Internal audit in the Railways, as distinct from the internal check built into day-to-day accounting, is best described as:

options.A: The statutory audit of railway accounts conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: An independent and periodical appraisal, conducted after the transactions have taken place, of the operations and records of a unit or office
options.C: The test check of measurements carried out by engineering officers on works
options.D: The continuous checking of transactions which forms part of the accounting process itself

q: A start-up recognised by DPIIT participates in a government procurement for a work. Under the General Financial Rules, such a start-up is exempted from:

options.A: Furnishing the performance guarantee after award of the work
options.B: Executing the formal agreement for the work
options.C: The criteria of prior turnover and prior experience, subject to its meeting the prescribed quality and technical specifications
options.D: Completing the work within the stipulated period

q: The third-party insurance which a works contractor is required to take out under the contract covers:

options.A: Liability for injury to third parties and damage to their property arising out of the execution of the work
options.B: Only loss or damage to the contractor's own plant and machinery
options.C: Only loss or damage to the work under execution
options.D: Only the contractor's own office premises and stores

q: In the measurement of reinforced cement concrete work executed under a contract:

options.A: The volume occupied by the reinforcement steel is deducted from the measurement of the concrete
options.B: Reinforcement steel is measured and paid for separately by weight, and no deduction is made from the measurement of the concrete for the volume of the steel
options.C: Reinforcement is paid for as a fixed percentage of the cost of the concrete
options.D: Reinforcement can be supplied and paid for only by the Railways

q: A bank guarantee furnished by a contractor towards earnest money, security deposit or performance guarantee for a works contract is acceptable to the Railways only when it is issued by:

options.A: Any co-operative bank of the district
options.B: A non-banking finance company
options.C: A foreign bank having no branch in India
options.D: A scheduled bank

q: A tenderer for a railway work has a near relative employed in a gazetted post in the railway organisation dealing with that work. In such a case, the tenderer is required to:

options.A: Withdraw his tender before its opening in all cases
options.B: Obtain the permission of the Railway Board before submitting the tender
options.C: Disclose this fact in his tender, failing which his tender is liable to be rejected
options.D: Quote his rates only through another enlisted firm

q: A number of petty repairs in a section are to be got done under the zonal contract already in force for the section. Each such repair is authorised and executed against:

options.A: Work orders issued by the Engineer under the zonal contract
options.B: Separate tenders invited for each petty work
options.C: Verbal instructions of the section engineer, without any written record
options.D: A separate formal agreement executed for each petty work

q: For a work executed on or near a running line, flagmen or watchmen are provided by the Railways for the protection of train movement during the execution of the work. The cost of providing them is:

options.A: Borne by the Railways as a safety measure in all cases
options.B: Recovered from the contractor executing the work
options.C: Shared equally between the Railways and the contractor
options.D: Charged to the contingencies of the estimate of the work

q: Railway land is allotted to a contractor for putting up a site camp and labour hutments in connection with a work. The correct position in respect of such land is that it is:

options.A: Transferred to the contractor for the duration of his business
options.B: Sold to the contractor at the market value of the land
options.C: Given free of all charges in every case
options.D: Given on licence, licence fee being recovered from him, and he must vacate and restore the land on completion of the work

q: At the time of disbursement of wages on a works contract, a contractor proposes to settle his workmen's wages in whatever manner suits him. The mode of payment required under the contract conditions is:

options.A: Only in cash, in the presence of the workmen's leader
options.B: Through the contractor's head office after the completion of the work
options.C: Through cheque or by crediting the wages to the bank accounts of the workmen
options.D: Partly in cash and partly in kind, as the contractor decides

q: Under the canons of financial propriety, an authority competent to sanction expenditure on a work should not exercise that power:

options.A: In a manner that directly or indirectly benefits the authority itself
options.B: Without obtaining the prior permission of the Railway Board in every case
options.C: At any time during the last quarter of the financial year
options.D: For any work which is to be executed through a contractor

q: A railway asset is damaged by a flood and its restoration is taken up as a work. The expenditure on the restoration is charged:

options.A: Wholly to Capital in all cases
options.B: To revenue as repairs, the element of improvement or betterment, if any, being charged to Capital or the appropriate fund head
options.C: To the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: To the contractor executing the restoration, as a penalty

q: A person is proposed as arbitrator in a dispute arising out of a works contract, but his relationship with one of the parties to the dispute falls within the Seventh Schedule of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The correct position is that:

options.A: He may act as arbitrator if the contractor has no objection to his appointment
options.B: He may act as arbitrator after disclosing the relationship to the tender committee
options.C: He is ineligible to be appointed as an arbitrator in that dispute
options.D: He is ineligible only if both the parties object to his appointment

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Interest is payable to a contractor on the earnest money and security deposit held by the Railways for the period for which they are held.
2. Deposits remaining unclaimed for more than three years after they have become refundable are credited to the revenues of the Railways as lapsed deposits.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Major railway projects which are beyond the powers of approval of the Railway Ministry are appraised, before investment approval by the Government, by:

options.A: The Public Accounts Committee
options.B: The Estimates Committee
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Public Investment Board

q: A zonal railway holds vacant land near a station which is not needed for operations for the present, and it is proposed to license the land temporarily to private parties for growing crops. This arrangement is known as:

options.A: 'Grow More Food' licensing
options.B: Land pooling with the adjoining landowners
options.C: Homestead leasing to railway staff
options.D: Orchard development licensing

q: Station buildings, platforms and circulating areas at a large number of stations all over the Railways are being modernised under one current scheme. That scheme is the:

options.A: Adarsh Station Scheme only
options.B: Model Station Scheme
options.C: Amrit Bharat Station Scheme
options.D: World-class Station Scheme

q: Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVC), which executes suburban railway projects in Mumbai, is:

options.A: A department of the Central Railway
options.B: A wholly-owned subsidiary of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority
options.C: A private company executing metro projects in Mumbai
options.D: A joint venture of the Ministry of Railways and the Government of Maharashtra

q: The subsoil at the site of a major bridge across a wide river consists of deep alluvial deposits. The type of foundation most commonly adopted for such a bridge is:

options.A: Open foundation
options.B: Raft foundation
options.C: Well foundation
options.D: Timber pile foundation

q: While designing a bridge across an alluvial stream, the engineer works out the waterway to be provided under the bridge and the likely depth of scour at its foundations. These are designed on the basis of:

options.A: Lacey's regime theory
options.B: The Manning formula alone
options.C: The discharge of the smallest recorded flood
options.D: The practice followed on the neighbouring road bridge

q: A newly erected traction installation is complete in all respects and is ready to be charged for regular use. Before it is energised, the sanction required is that of:

options.A: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.B: The Electrical Inspector to the Government of India
options.C: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation
options.D: The Railway Board

q: A section engineer holds a small stock of permanent way materials with him as imprest stock, instead of drawing every item from the stores depot. The purpose of holding such stock is:

options.A: For sale to contractors working in the section
options.B: For use only on new construction works of the division
options.C: As a reserve to be opened only on the orders of the General Manager
options.D: For meeting urgent day-to-day maintenance requirements without waiting for a regular issue from the stores depot

q: During periodical inspections, the engineering staff notice several unauthorised occupations of railway land in the section. For watching these cases and pursuing their removal, they are systematically recorded in:

options.A: The Measurement Book of the section
options.B: The Works Register of the division
options.C: The Encroachment Register maintained for the section
options.D: The Fixed Asset Register of the Railway

q: The design of the foundations of a major bridge is to be finalised, for which reliable data on the nature, strata and bearing capacity of the sub-soil at the site is needed. Such data is obtained by:

options.A: Carrying out bore-hole exploration (geotechnical investigation) at the site
options.B: Examining the oldest bridge in the vicinity of the site
options.C: Referring to the district gazetteer of the area
options.D: Testing the river water for its salinity

q: In the track records of a section, the term 'sleeper density' used for a length of track denotes:

options.A: The weight of one sleeper in kilograms
options.B: The depth of ballast provided below the sleepers
options.C: The spacing between two adjacent tracks
options.D: The number of sleepers provided per unit length of the track
